newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's air carriers to boost international fares.
newsitem.headline: Japan's air carriers to boost international fares.

text.p: Japan's major air carriers announced plans on Wednesday to boost international airfares by three percent due to surging fuel costs.

Japan Airlines Co Ltd (JAL), All Nippon Airways Co Ltd (ANA) and Japan Air System Co Ltd said they had asked the Ministry of Transportation for permission to increase fares, starting from December 15.
If approved, the standard price for a round-trip economy-class ticket for flights between Tokyo and Los Angeles, for example, would rise by about 11,000 yen ($95) to 353,100 yen ($3,150).
The airlines hope to raise airfares on a total of 127 international routes.
The proposed increase is based on a November 15 agreement at the International Air Transport Association (IATA), an industry organisation based in Geneva.
IATA members have agreed to increase fares in the hope of passing on the recent rises in fuel costs to passengers.
ANA said last month when it announced its earnings for the half year to September 30 that the cost of fuel in the six-month period rose nine percent year-on-year.
It also expects fuel costs for the full year to March 31 will increase by 10 billion yen ($89.2 million) from the previous year.
